data.body:
LANDED AND CLOSED 2026-08-09.

The finished work had been sitting as unpushed commit 036ca3c16d in worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-9416, which was 379 commits behind origin/main. Rather than rebase that stack, the single commit was cherry-picked onto a fresh worktree at origin/main (one conflict, docs/env-vars.md, resolved by taking HEAD and regenerating with scripts/gen_env_registry.py since that file is generated and drift-gated).

Gerrit change 1571. Patch set 1 took LLM-Review +1 but Verified -1: the MODULE-SIZE GATE failed because src/rebar/_config_schema.py was already exactly at the 800-LOC hard cap on main, so this change's +9 net comment lines pushed it to 809. Patch set 2 compressed the new explanatory comments (the durable documentation for this key lives in docs/config.md, which this change adds) to land the file at exactly 800. Verified +1 and LLM-Review +1 on patch set 2; submitted and merged as 74a7332606.

Verification at the merged commit, run in a worktree venv built from that tree: 'grep -rni overlap_enabled src rebar.toml' returns exactly the four expected back-compat sites (the _ALIASES entry, both _deprecations rows, and the _LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES key) and zero lines in rebar.toml; docs/config.md carries both the inventory entry and the Back-compat env rename row; the five named test modules pass 54/54; make lint and make typecheck clean.

Note for anyone re-running these: the tests MUST be run from a venv installed against the tree under test. Running them against a checkout whose editable install points at a pre-rename source produces 18 spurious failures.

Cross-reference: this landing is direct evidence for story 5e53 (module-size headroom exhausted) — an unrelated 9-line comment addition was blocked by the cap.
